title: Menu items that are settings wear a checkmark instead of rewording themselves
goal: Show Grid changes its wording to Hide Grid when the grid is on, and Snap to Grid becomes Stop Snapping to Grid. That is how an action is written, not a setting. Every menu item that is simply on or off should keep one name and carry a checkmark when it is on, so you can see the state without reading a sentence, and so the item does not move under the pointer as its label changes length. That goes for all of them, panels and the history included, not just the grid.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-05, then confirmed for ALL stateful items rather than just the grid, so no per item judgement is needed: convert every one. No menu item in the app uses a checkmark today. EditorCommands.swift flips titles at line 527 (grid), 536 (snapping), 492 (layers panel) and 503 (Library), and MainMenuTitles.swift retitles the history item from a separate file. That history item is reached from the menu bar agent as well as the editor and there is an open task about the two disagreeing (show-history-and-hide-history-agree-with-whether); read it first and make sure this change resolves rather than deepens it. SwiftUI menu items take a Toggle for exactly this, which also reports the right state to accessibility, rather than drawing a tick by hand. Leave true actions alone, for example Play and Pause at line 183 and Crop to Region at 198.
acceptance: Every menu item that holds an on or off state keeps a single name and carries a checkmark when it is on: the grid, snapping, the layers panel, the Library and the history, plus any other found while doing it
No menu item is left flipping its wording to say what state it is in; the audit lists every item changed and confirms none were missed
An item that genuinely performs an action, such as playing or pausing, is left alone, and the audit says which those are
Each one still works from its keyboard shortcut, and the shortcut is shown once rather than moving between two items
The history item reads the same in the menu bar agent and in the editor window, since it is retitled from a second place
Nothing changes about what any of them does
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the View menu and the history item in both states, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: inventory of every menu item in the app that is simply on or off, so nothing is missed: View > Show/Hide Grid (EditorCommands 528), View > Snap to Grid / Stop Snapping to Grid (545), View > Show/Hide Layers (492), View > Show/Hide Library (503), Capture > Show/Hide History (EditorCommands 159 and PhotonzApp 198, one name in CaptureMenuNames), and two row context menus in LayersPanel: a layer's Hide/Show and Unlock/Lock (1823-4) and a measurement row's Hide/Show (2168). Seven items.

left alone deliberately, all actions rather than settings: Play/Pause (183), Crop to Region / Finish Crop (198), Record Screen / Video... / Stop Recording (CaptureMenuNames.recording - the two do different things and the first opens a picker), Copy Measurement / Copy Measurements (480, pluralisation not state), Show All Measurements and Hide All Measurements (both offered at once, each dimmed when it would change nothing), Check for Updates... / Checking for Updates... (progress, not a setting).

adversarial review before building. The name each item keeps: the Show form, so Show Grid, Show Layers, Show Library, Show History and Snap to Grid, with a checkmark when on. Reasons: it is the name that is already there so nothing has to be relearned or re-found; the grid settings popover already draws these same two switches as checkboxes called Show grid and Snap to grid (CanvasGridCopy), so the menu and the popover now agree word for word; and a bare noun (Grid) sitting next to Grid Settings... in the View menu says less than the verb does. The two row menus get the adjective instead, Visible and Locked, because a bare Show on a row means nothing.

adversarial review, the risk worth naming: a checkmark can go stale exactly the way the title did. SwiftUI re-runs a Commands body only while handling an event, and a shortcut press rebuilds it from the state BEFORE the item's action runs (proven 2026-09-04, see MainMenuTitles). So the history item keeps its imperative correction, writing state on/off onto the live item instead of a title. The View items are window scoped and cannot be read live in a probe walk at all (PlaytestHarness.frozenMenuBar: a background app's window commands are dimmed and frozen from launch), so their proof is the build plus core tests, and the audit will say so rather than claim a live reading.

shortest version that delivers the value: a SwiftUI Toggle per item, which draws the checkmark and reports the state to accessibility, plus one place in PhotonzCore naming every on/off item so a test can hold the line that none of them flips. Nothing decorative to cut.

built: seven items are SwiftUI Toggles now. MenuToggleNames (PhotonzCore, 5 tests) names every on/off item in one place and a test refuses any name starting with Hide, Stop or Un. CaptureMenuNames.history lost its isShown: parameter; MainMenuTitles became MainMenuState and writes item.state onto the live item rather than a title, so the history item keeps the correction that stopped it being a toggle behind.

one thing found in the review of the built thing and fixed: every binding's set FLIPS the live reading rather than storing the value SwiftUI hands it. A Commands body is re-run only while an event is handled, so the value an item was DRAWN from can be a toggle behind, and storing !stale is a press that does nothing. Flipping the live reading is what the plain Button did.

acceptance 4, 5 and 6 verified live: Scripts/playtest/menu-checkmarks-walk.json photographs the real Capture menu with Show History unticked and ticked, and the real View menu in three states, asserting every tick. Both shortcut steps assert the checkmark BEFORE the press, so the shortcut path is proven too. history-menu-title-walk.json now asserts the checkmark in all four readings including the Esc dismissal, and both walks fail against a lying tick (proven by inverting an assertion).

harness work this needed, all additive and documented in docs/design/playtest-harness.md: a menuShot step that opens one of our own menu bar menus over the probe window and photographs it, which is the first time anything here could SHOW a menu (a menu draws outside the process, so an offscreen render is blank); ticked/unticked assertions on it, which refuse a row with no action behind it because that row's state is a default rather than the document's; a checked field on shortcut; and showGrid/hideGrid actions that SET rather than flip.

two findings about reading a live menu, worth keeping: a window scoped row reads the real document once ANY of the app's windows is key, and the Capture History overlay takes key, so a walk that wants a live View menu opens it first and leaves it up. And makeKey() on the editor window is worse than nothing: it takes key AWAY from whatever had it and leaves the whole bar reading defaults.

not verified live, and said so in the audit: the two row context menus (Visible, Locked). A right click menu is still out of a walk's reach. They use the same Toggle as the four View rows that ARE photographed. Follow-up filed: a-scripted-walk-can-open-and-photograph-a-right.

3399 tests green. Ten walks re-run green: menu-checkmarks, history-menu-title, history-tooltips, menu-bar, undo-shortcut, canvas-grid, grid-surround-snap, grid-settings, library, redline. Nothing is forked into Next, so all seven items are shared code and Next has the change by construction.

Seven menu items that are simply on or off keep one name and wear a checkmark now: View's Show Layers, Show Library, Show Grid and Snap to Grid, Capture's Show History in both menus, and a layer row's Visible and Locked. Each is a SwiftUI Toggle, so accessibility hears the state too; MenuToggleNames (PhotonzCore) names them all and a test refuses any name that announces its own state; MainMenuState writes the true state onto the live history item, keeping the fix that stopped it being a toggle behind. Actions were left alone (Play/Pause, Crop to Region, Record/Stop Recording) and the audit says which. Verified live: a new menuShot step photographs the real Capture and View menus and asserts every tick, and both walks fail against a lying tick. 3399 tests green, ten walks green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-05-menu-checkmarks.json
